Dear Editor-in-Chief,

We submit for your consideration the manuscript entitled **"Wearable Electrochemical Sensing Systems Based on Microneedle Arrays: A Full-Chain Review from Sensor Fabrication to Intelligent Embedded Terminals"** for publication as a Review Article in *Biosensors and Bioelectronics*.

**Scope and Contribution**

Wearable microneedle array (MNA)-based electrochemical sensing has emerged as a transformative platform for continuous, minimally invasive interstitial fluid (ISF) monitoring. Despite rapid advances across individual subsystems, no existing review has addressed this technology as a complete engineering system. Our review fills this gap by treating MNA-based wearable electrochemical sensing as a five-layer engineering chain — fabrication → electrochemical transduction → biomarker detection → circuit integration → embedded intelligence — systematically analyzed in 91 peer-reviewed papers from 2021 to 2026.

Specifically, this review makes the following contributions not found in any prior work:

1. **Full-chain integration perspective**: Explicit analysis of how fabrication choices (electrode sensitivity, geometry) propagate into AFE circuit specifications, which in turn constrain deployable AI model complexity — a chain logic not addressed in any prior review.
2. **Clinical accuracy benchmarking**: Systematic application of Clarke Error Grid Analysis, MARD benchmarks, and ISO 15197 criteria to compare MNA-WES performance against commercial CGM devices (Dexcom G7: MARD 8.2%; Abbott FreeStyle Libre 2: MARD 9.7%), quantifying the 1–2 percentage point translation gap.
3. **Embedded intelligence coverage**: The only review to cover on-device signal processing, ML-based adaptive calibration, edge AI inference (including INT8-quantized LSTM on ARM Cortex-M4), and closed-loop therapeutic feedback for MNA-based systems.
4. **Regulatory pathway guidance**: Comprehensive analysis of FDA 510(k)/De Novo pathways, EU IVDR 2022/746 Class D requirements, and ISO 10993 biocompatibility testing — enabling researchers to design translation-ready MNA systems.
5. **Transparent citation audit**: All specific numerical claims are tagged as [V] (DOI-verified) or [N] (needs verification), providing readers with an explicit evidence quality map.

**Journal Fit**

This manuscript directly aligns with *Biosensors and Bioelectronics*' focus on integrated sensing systems and clinical translation. The journal has published foundational work cited in this review, including Tehrani et al. (2022) and Yang et al. (2023, 2024). The full-chain integration perspective complements the component-level reviews the journal has published in 2022–2023, providing the system-level synthesis the field now requires.

**Ethics and Declarations**

- This manuscript has not been published elsewhere, is not under simultaneous consideration by another journal, and all authors have approved the submission.
